annotations.text: De Morgan's law is not a separate axiom in EG — it falls out of how disjunction is drawn. ¬P∨¬Q is ~[ ~[¬P] ~[¬Q] ], and ¬¬X is X under a double cut, so ¬(P∧Q) = ~[ (P)(Q) ] becomes ¬P∨¬Q by growing a double cut around each conjunct.
Two DC+ moves, each meaning-preserving (a double cut adds nothing). The equivalence runs both ways: DC- twice returns the conjunction.
